items.stem: Backups are accessed a few times a year but must be retrievable within milliseconds when needed. Which storage class best balances cost and access?

options.rationale: Correct: Glacier Instant Retrieval offers low-cost storage with millisecond access for rarely read data.
Standard costs more and targets frequent access.
Deep Archive is cheapest but retrieval takes hours, not milliseconds.
EBS is block storage for instances, not an S3 class.

items.explanation: Correct: Glacier Instant Retrieval fits rarely accessed data that still needs instant retrieval.

items.stem: Which TWO grant temporary or scoped access without making a bucket public? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Generate a presigned URL for a specific object
options.rationale: Correct: a presigned URL grants time-limited access to one object.

options.text: Attach a least-privilege IAM policy to the principal
options.rationale: Correct: IAM policies scope access to named identities.

options.text: Disable Block Public Access and allow public reads
options.rationale: That makes the bucket public, the opposite of least privilege.

options.text: Set an ACL granting AllUsers read
options.rationale: Granting AllUsers exposes the data publicly.

items.explanation: Correct: presigned URLs and least-privilege IAM both avoid public exposure.

items.stem: To recover objects after an accidental delete, what must be enabled on the bucket beforehand?

options.rationale: Correct: versioning retains prior versions so deletes can be undone.
Storage class affects cost, not delete recovery.
Acceleration speeds transfers, unrelated to recovery.
Requester Pays shifts cost; it does not protect against deletes.

items.explanation: Correct: bucket versioning is required to recover deleted objects.
